description: Senior-skewed cruise passenger composition for the NORO-AGE-FOOD-01 demographic arms. Every passenger class draws a weighted age-band composition rather than the repository default's uniform bands; crew classes draw the measured Diamond Princess crew composition.

published_inputs: diamond_princess_2020.json's whole-ship derivation (NIID Field Briefing 20 Feb 2020 decadal counts; Tsuboi 2020 DOI 10.35772/ghm.2020.01037 per-role means: passengers 66.0, crew 36.6). The passenger_general weights below are that file's derived passenger composition verbatim — the only measured cruise-ship age composition in the repository.
The 65-74/75+ split inside passenger_elderly reuses the same derived counts (969.0 / 734.5).
steps: passenger_general inherits the Diamond Princess passenger band composition unchanged: a senior-market hull is modelled as the measured senior cruise population rather than an invented one.
passenger_elderly is kept as a class (compliance_by_class still differentiates it) but draws the DP >=65 sub-composition (65-74 vs 75+ at 969:734.5).
passenger_family on a senior-market hull is declared, not measured: weights carry mostly adults with a small child share (child 0.10). Grade C declared.
All crew classes draw the DP-derived crew composition (18-34 / 35-49 / 50-64 at 0.50/0.35/0.15, reproducing published crew mean 36.6).
refusals: No weight is chosen to move posting, incidence or attack-rate outputs; the only measured input is the DP composition, and every other weight is labelled Grade C declared.

Composite passenger composition under the shipped class fractions (general 0.50 / family 0.10 / elderly 0.10 of a 0.70 passenger share): ~60% of passengers >=65, ~2% under 18 — versus ~14% and ~5% on the default bundle. The composite is stated, not hidden inside the per-class tables.
